correctness.summary: Indexer computes the byte offset as index * UnsafeUtility.SizeOf<T>() in 32-bit int arithmetic, overflowing for valid in-range indices when index*sizeof(T) exceeds 2^31, yielding a wrong pointer and out-of-buffer access.
correctness.triggeringInput: NativeArray<long> arr = new NativeArray<long>(300_000_000, allocator); long v = arr[300_000_000 - 1]; // (300000000-1)*8 overflows Int32
correctness.rootCause: var byteOffset = _buffer + index * UnsafeUtility.SizeOf<T>() (lines 46 and 52). index * SizeOf<T>() is int*int; for index*size >= 2^31 it wraps to a negative/incorrect value before the IntPtr addition, so the access targets memory outside the allocation even though index < _length. The constructor itself correctly uses (long)length, confirming such large arrays are intended to be representable.
correctness.suggestedFix: Widen before multiplying: var byteOffset = _buffer + (IntPtr)((long)index * UnsafeUtility.SizeOf<T>()); in both the getter and setter.

perf.summary: Indexer recomputes UnsafeUtility.SizeOf<T>() inline (fine) but uses IntPtr arithmetic with int index that can be strength-reduced; minor consistency note.
perf.currentCost: byteOffset = _buffer + index * UnsafeUtility.SizeOf<T>(). SizeOf<T>() folds to a constant under Burst so index*const becomes a shift for power-of-two T - already good. The only cost is using Unsafe.Read/Write through a reconstructed (void*) each access.
perf.proposedChange: Optionally expose the element access via ((T*)_buffer)[index] which lets the compiler do typed scaled-index addressing (mov [base + idx*scale]) directly instead of manual byte math plus Unsafe.Read. Functionally identical, often one fewer cast/temp.
perf.rationale: Typed pointer indexing emits a single scaled-index load/store and avoids the IntPtr-to-void* round-trip, slightly shorter dependency chain. Burst typically lowers both to the same code, so impact is low, but it is cleaner and never worse.
perf.risk: None functionally; ((T*)_buffer)[index] is equivalent to the byte-offset Read/Write for unmanaged T. Keep _buffer as IntPtr or cache the T* - behavior identical.
